links.outcome: Readability grade level of chatbot responses versus recommended 6th-8th grade
links.effect: Significant differences between chatbots (Gunning Fox p = 0.008, Flesch-Kincaid p < 0.001); all responses required education levels above the recommended 6th-8th grade.
links.quote: A significant difference was found between chatbots in terms of readability scores (Gunning Fox Index p = 0.008, Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level p < 0.001), with all responses requiring education levels above the recommended 6th-8th grade.

links.outcome: Plain-language comprehensibility (readability) of chatbot patient education responses
links.effect: All chatbot responses required education levels above the recommended 6th-8th grade; readability differed across chatbots (FKGL p < 0.001).
links.quote: AI chatbots show potential for patient education but produce content with readability levels too complex for general audiences.

screen.reason: The study evaluates the readability and quality of responses from four commercial LLMs to standardized overactive bladder patient questions evaluated by expert urologists, but does not test a specific deployment safeguard or practice intervention.
